newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms to launch satellite in Fla.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms to launch satellite in Fla.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc's Tempo Satellite Inc said on Tuesday it plans to launch one of its direct broadcast satellites (DBS) from Cape Canaveral, Florida in February.
Earlier Tuesday the Federal Communications Commission denied a bid by TCI and Telquest Ventures to beam television programs across the United States from a Canadian orbital satellite slot.
The two U.S. companies wanted to use two satellites that had not yet been licensed by Canada and that would be owned and operated by a Canadian corporation, Telsat Canada.
TCI said it is considering options for the second satellite. It will be a back up for the February launch.
TCI said the satellite is the only uncommitted DBS satellite in the world and that there should be a "ready market" for it if TCI's Tempo chooses not to use it.
Tempo is in discussions with Primestar, a DBS provider, to use the satellite to provide a high-powered DBS service throughout the continental United States, Alaska and Hawaii.
